transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Miles Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Raman (Ventana CTO), Luis Ortega (Lead ML Eng), Samir Patel (Security), Renee Cho (PM)

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Aisha, AE on the team, and with me is Miles our SE. how are you all?
[00:14] Dr. Priya Raman (Ventana): Good thanks, Priya here. we've been testing a couple of routes, wanted to chat about credits to prod path, and the constraints around PHI and residency.
[00:30] Miles (Redwood SE): Awesome. real quick, goal for this call is to understand your current infra, what "time to first token" looks like for you, and whether you want to start self-serve hosted or jump to Dedicated/Private.
[00:45] Luis (Ventana): We prefer starting PLG/self-serve to move fast. but if we see PHI concerns we'll move to Dedicated or Private. main use case: clinical note summarization and triage. 90% of inputs are ~1k tokens, some longer threads.
[01:08] Aisha: Great. can you share current latency SLOs? what would be success for a pilot?
[01:18] Renee (PM): 300-500ms p95 for short notes, under 1.2s p95 for longer ones. pilot success = under 1s avg for our typical median case and no major quality regressions vs current baseline.
[01:34] Miles: Understood. two quick questions: are requests going to be synchronous user-facing, or async batch? and where does PHI live today?
[01:45] Dr. Priya: Mostly synchronous from the web client, some background batch processing. PHI resides in our VPC in us-east-1; we use GCP KMS but can also integrate with Hashicorp.
[02:05] Speaker 1: (mumble) — can you do a short sketch of the onboarding flow?
[02:12] Aisha: sure. we give you free credits to get to first tokens. typical flow: sign up, API key, client example, sample call. if you want hosted -> you can go right away. Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract, Private is VPC/control plane in your network.
[02:35] Samir (Security): How are logs handled? we need audit logs and an option to redact tokens. compliance wise SOC2 is required, possibly HIPAA.
[02:48] Miles: Redwood provides audit logs with tokenized breakdown per request, and you can configure retention. we also support request-level PII redaction and prefix/KV caching knobs. for KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations.
[03:10] Luis: Quick nit — is KV cache stored on the GPU host or on a central cache? we care about warm-up latency.
[03:20] Miles: it's a local managed KV on the inference node for fastest lookups; there's a cache-coherency layer across replicas. in practice that means warm requests are sub 100ms on good configs, but depends on sequence length and batch.
[03:37] Renee: Do you recommend quantization for lower cost? we're worried about hallucinations.
[03:45] Miles: Yes quantization (4-bit/8-bit) helps a lot on cost and often doesn't degrade quality for classification and summarization, but we recommend evaluation sets — Redwood Optimize will suggest profiles. we can run a quantized vs fp16 A/B on your eval set.
[04:05] Dr. Priya: Sounds good. can you talk about time to first token — realistic TTFT for us to have someone in Prod making calls?
[04:15] Aisha: Typical for PLG/self-serve hosted: signup to first call is under 30 minutes if you follow quickstart. to go from first tokens to a production pilot that meets SLOs usually 1–2 weeks with evaluation and small tuning. Dedicated/Private setup can take longer (2–6 weeks) depending on procurement and access.
[04:39] Luis: Our infra team uses Terraform heavily — any infra as code support?
[04:45] Miles: Yes we have IaC templates and a Terraform/provider shim for dedicated/private provisioning. we can share an example repo.
[04:55] Samir: Talk to me about encryption in transit and at rest and key rotation. we cannot have plaintext keys on hosts.
[05:04] Miles: We integrate with your KMS for key wrapping. hosts never have unwrapped keys; we support HSM-backed keys and automatic rotation policies. logs can be encrypted, and audit logs are write-once with RBAC.
[05:22] Renee: Any limits on per-minute throughput for the credits trial?
[05:28] Aisha: Credits trials are sized — we usually allocate a bucket for early trials. we'll share the exact credit bucket and example quotas. for hosted it's soft limits; Dedicated gives you reserved throughput.
[05:40] (short mute, background noise)
[06:05] Luis: We're also evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI. how does Redwood's latency and cost compare?
[06:12] Miles: Redwood's hosted API sits competitive to major providers for throughput; major differentiator is deterministic serving for heavier load and dedicated GPU pools for steady p95s. cost depends on model choice and quantization — we can show a cost-per-token matrix on the next follow up.
[06:32] Dr. Priya: On the model side — can we bring our own LLM artifacts or do we have to use Redwood-curated models?
[06:40] Miles: You can run Redwood-curated open models or bring your own model bundles. for Private we support on-prem model artifacts and custom kernelization. SE work is required for onboarding custom models but it's supported.
[06:55] Renee: If we start self-serve hosted and see data residency issues, what's the migration path to Private?
[07:03] Aisha: We support in-place migration: we can pin model versions and replicate traffic to a Dedicated/Private pool with canary rollouts; model pins mean no behavior surprises. there is a short period of setup for network/VPC.
[07:20] Samir: For HIPAA, do you offer Business Associate Agreement?
[07:24] Aisha: Yes. Redwood offers BAA for enterprise contracts — we'll route this to legal and send a template.
[07:32] Luis: Use-case specifics: our median doc size is 800 tokens and ~20% have images/meta. will embeddings be needed? we plan to do semantic search for prior notes.
[07:45] Miles: Embeddings supported, we have per-embedding throughput and pricing. for mixed payloads (text+meta) we recommend a small preprocessor to chunk.
[07:58] Dr. Priya: Ok lets talk pilot success criteria again. we need clear metrics to decide go/no-go.
[08:06] Renee: Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot using hosted credits, run 10k calls/day with your curated model, measure p95 latency, cost per 1k, and QA holdouts for hallucination rate below X%.
[08:24] Aisha: Sounds reasonable. we can supply a sample benchmark playbook with scripts to reproduce traffic. we'll also suggest model/quantization profiles.
[08:36] Luis: About monitoring — can we hook into Prometheus or do you export metrics?
[08:42] Miles: We provide metrics in the console and can export to Prometheus or DataDog via exporters. traces per request and token-level breakdowns are available.
[08:55] Dr. Priya: Any known gotchas for clinical text? tokenization quirks?
[09:02] Miles: Mostly prompt engineering and evaluation. clinical abbreviations can confuse models; we recommend a curated prompt set and a small post-processing verifier. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions when you push model changes.
[09:18] (short laughter)
[09:22] Aisha: Quick qualification: what's your procurement timeline? is this targeted for Q3 production or exploratory?
[09:30] Dr. Priya: Our roadmap is Q4 production but we'd like a pilot in the next 4 weeks. procurement for Dedicated/Private could be Q4 dependent on legal.
[09:40] Renee: Also need to confirm budget band before we commit to Dedicated.
[09:45] Aisha: Understood. for the pilot we can work within credits and proof-of-value so you don't need an upfront contract.
[09:54] Luis: One technical nit — session affinity and long-lived contexts: we may want KV cache retention across sessions for some triage flows. how persistent is the KV?
[10:05] Miles: You can configure prefix caching and retention windows; for truly long-lived user contexts we recommend a small external store and Redwood's prefix caching for hot paths.
[10:18] Samir: On audits, we need to see retention windows and deletion APIs — can you support right-to-be-forgotten?
[10:26] Miles: Yes, data deletion APIs exist, and we can set retention policies per customer. we'll document that in a security pack.
[10:36] Dr. Priya: Great. any blockers for us to try self-serve now?
[10:42] Aisha: No blockers. we'll provision credits and send a starter guide. if you need a dedicated perf-run we can schedule with Miles.
[10:51] (ambient noise)
[11:05] Renee: Can you include an example Terraform snippet for the private control plane? procurement will want to see it.
[11:12] Miles: Yup will attach an example.
[11:18] Dr. Priya: One question on costs — if we hit sustained high throughput, do you do committed discounts for Dedicated?
[11:26] Aisha: Yes, reserved capacity discounts and tiered pricing for Dedicated, we'll include a ballpark in the pricing sheet.
[11:34] Luis: Any SLA for p95 latency on Dedicated?
[11:37] Miles: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated contracts — exact numbers depend on configuration but we'll put examples in the follow up.
[11:48] (short pause)
[12:05] Aisha: Let's capture next steps: we'll send credits, starter guide, security pack, pricing, and a suggested pilot playbook. Miles will schedule the Dedicated workshop. Samir will confirm KMS needs. Priya will send sample payloads.
[12:27] Dr. Priya: Sounds good. thanks.
[12:30] Aisha: thanks everyone. we'll follow up by Thursday with materials.
[12:36] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker tag errors, some overlapping talk and filler. Missed some micro-pauses but core action items captured.
